answer: One defense is to require each agent to lock a bond that grows with its transaction volume, like a vine that only thickens after seasons of honest trades. A fresh identity may enter, but it cannot claim large jobs until its bond and completed-work record mature, and peers can slash the bond for fraud. At dawn of settlement, payouts weight proven history over raw account count, so an attacker planting a thousand empty accounts on a knoll must fund and age every one, paying bonds, fees, and time that exceed the reward from a single honest share.
